interest: Japanese territorial ambitions 1933–37, island sovereignty queries and Shirase's Antarctic bays.
overview: This State Department file (decimal file 894.014, covering January 1933 through November 1937) compiles diplomatic cross-reference sheets, despatches, memoranda, diplomatic notes, and official correspondence concerning the territorial status, boundaries, and expansionist ambitions of the Japanese Empire. The materials document international anxieties over Japanese outward pressure following its withdrawal from the League of Nations, tracking reported Japanese interests in Soviet Kamchatka, Dutch East Indian oil and timber concessions in Borneo, Portuguese Timor and Macau, New Guinea, and Australia's Northern Territory, as well as an alleged clandestine effort to purchase hereditary Brunei title deeds to the Philippine islands of Palawan, Balabac, and Cagayan. In addition, the file contains extensive documentation addressing cartographic and sovereignty determinations handled by the State Department Geographer and the Office of the Historical Adviser—notably regarding Marcus Island, the Bonin Islands, and historical inquiries from private citizens and the National Geographic Society regarding whether the Kurile Islands were ever occupied under the United States flag. The file also preserves diplomatic correspondence surrounding Lieutenant Nobu Shirase's 1912 Antarctic expedition and Admiral Richard E. Byrd's cartographic recognition of Japanese polar discoveries, an authoritative State Department chronological memorandum detailing Japanese territorial annexations from 1874 to 1935, and reports on Premier Fumimaro Konoye's promotional campaign for a 'United States of Asia'.

subfiles.about: A citizen inquiry and research memorandum asking whether the United States ever temporarily occupied and held any of the Kuril Islands.

subfiles.to: Mahlon F. Perkins, Acting Historical Adviser

subfiles.about: An official State Department reply informing R. Charlton Wright that records show no historical U.S. occupation of the Kuril Islands.

subfiles.summary: Mahlon F. Perkins tells R. Charlton Wright that no records show the Kurile Islands were ever held by the United States.
subfiles.title: Letter from Mahlon F. Perkins to R. Charlton Wright denying any U.S. occupation of the Kuril Islands

subfiles.about: An editorial inquiry from the National Geographic Society regarding alleged historical U.S. possession of the Kuril Islands.
